A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SpecAgent study. Their text, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial appendix expansion and reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original REPOCOD-based code-completion experiments, including pass@1, latency, component ablations, and experiments with different agent backbones.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds LLM-judged analyses of retrieval successes and failures in Appendix G.

M1.justification: The retriever–forecaster combination, cached contexts, and main nine-retrieval/three-prediction composition remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 and Appendix B document the existing procedure more explicitly; they do not establish an implemented method revision.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same REPOCOD-based function-completion coverage: 980 problems from 11 repositories, with the retained indexing-time and inference-time scenarios. Appendix G analyzes cases from this existing benchmark.

E2.justification: The SpecAgent comparisons retain no context, BM25, RepoMap, BM25 + RepoMap, UniXcoder, CodeSage v2 large, and the oracle. Appendix G separately analyzes BM25 and RepoMap against an earlier oracle without adding a competitor to the SpecAgent evaluations.

E3.justification: Appendix G adds a diagnostic protocol selecting cases where only one retrieval method yields a passing completion. Claude 3.7 Sonnet judges failure causes, context helpfulness, and context decisiveness using an explicitly earlier oracle. This supplements the retained benchmark evaluation.

E4.justification: The existing ablations and examples are retained. New Appendix G adds systematic BM25/oracle and RepoMap/oracle failure analyses, success-factor breakdowns, and detailed cases examining missing dependencies, type information, usage examples, and repository conventions.

E5.justification: V2 newly documents confidence outputs: a 0–1 self-assessment from the function-removal scorer and high/medium/low confidence from the diagnostic judge (B.6 and G.1). These are agent judgments; calibration, confidence intervals, and repeated-run uncertainty for benchmark scores remain unreported.

E6.justification: Appendix G adds judge-reported context-decisiveness rates: 98.8% versus 25.5% for oracle/BM25 and 97.8% versus 41.7% for oracle/RepoMap, plus helpfulness findings and case outcomes. For Qwen3-8B with the Qwen3-Coder agent, reported latency changes from 39.99 seconds to 3.80 seconds (v1 Table 5; v2 Table 8). Existing pass@1 values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1 introduces notation for the already-described context composition and caching procedure. No substantive mathematical definitions, assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and summary retain the same contributions and claims about speculative indexing-time context, future-context leakage, and approximately 9–11 percentage-point accuracy gains.

C2.justification: Appendix G adds substantial interpretations of baseline failures involving lexical mismatch, missing implementations and usage information, and multi-hop dependencies. Section 4.1 adds cache-refresh and cost-amortization considerations. The original limitations and risk discussions are retained.

D1.justification: New Appendix B supplies agent prompts, tool workflows, parsing, caching, deterministic composition, oracle filtering, and validation details. Appendix H newly specifies decoding parameters, retrieval chunk and candidate limits, exploration budgets, and serving settings. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: The related-work text and bibliography are unchanged after accounting for reflow. The positioning relative to code models, repository retrieval, and indexing-time computation remains the same.

P1.justification: The original main narrative and retained appendix prose are largely unchanged. V2 adds an appendix contents page, dedicated sections, updated cross-references, and localized method and deployment explanations while preserving the existing narrative order.

P2.justification: V2 changes the appendix from full-width single-column pages to a continuous two-column layout, reflowing code listings and tables. It adds Algorithm 1 and Figures 4–5, redraws Figure 2 while retaining its example, and rearranges the Appendix A tables.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses an important reproducibility gap by supplying previously missing agent prompts, execution details, and experimental parameters in Appendices B and H. Appendix G also makes the explanatory arguments more inspectable. Its earlier, privileged oracle limits direct conclusions about SpecAgent, but the documentation gains substantially improve the paper despite unchanged headline accuracy results.
